text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- President Glafcos Clerides stresses there is no reason for concern after rumours the Turks will attempt to cause incidents in Cyprus.
- The European Parliament is expected to freeze European Union funds to Ankara today in a resolution prompted by the situation in Cyprus and the killing of two Greek Cypriots by Turks in Dherinia.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Arms race in Cyprus is cause of 'grave concern', says the United Nations.
- Arab convicts could serve prison terms in their own countries under draft legislation.
- Profits up at Popular Bank.
- Island's potato board to introduce export quotas to better monitor production.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Laiki (Popular Bank) reports moderate H1 profit rise.
- Pay TV LTV subscribers reach 22.000.
- Price of imported cheese set to rise.
- Deal for local Carlsberg brewers to take over Pepsi franchise fizzles out.
HARAVGHI
- The government has to clarify to the public whether rumours circulating on a Turkish-provoked incident can be substantiated, says communist Akel leader Demetris Christofias.
- Popular Bank chairman Kikis Lazarides paints bleak outlook for the island's economy.
- House of Representatives is to debate a bill adding limitations to the transfer of property to foreigners.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Tension on the island has been relatively defused after American intervention.
- Centre-right Diko will seek support either from communist Akel or right-wing Disy to back bid by Spyros Kyprianou for presidency in 1998.
- Wife of Tasos Isaak, killed by the Turks in Dherinia last month, gives birth to a girl, Anastassia.
SIMERINI
- The United States and Britain are putting pressure on Russia to suspend its military supplies to Cyprus.
- Public to pay two million pounds for every kilometre in the third phase of the Paphos-Limassol road.
